items.stem: The resistance of the metal coil in a resistance thermometer is 70 Ω at 30 °C and 80 Ω at 50 °C. What is the resistance of the metal coil if it is placed in boiling water? Assume that the resistance of the coil varies linearly with temperature.
items.hint:
Let the resistance of the metal coil at 100 °C be x.
(x − 70)/(80 − 70) = (100 − 30)/(50 − 30)
x = 105 Ω.

items.stem: The graphs below show the variation of the electrical resistance R of four circuit elements with temperature T. Which of the circuit elements is the most suitable for measuring temperature?

options.text: R increases with T, and the graph curves upwards.

image.alt: R increases with T, and the graph curves upwards.

options.text: R increases with T, and the graph curves downwards.

image.alt: R increases with T, and the graph curves downwards.

options.text: R does not change with T.

image.alt: R does not change with T.

items.hint: The electrical resistance R of the circuit element varies linearly with the temperature T. The thermometer making use of the variation of R can have a linear scale which is the most suitable.
